/-!
# Prime quadruplets

A prime quadruplet is a set of four primes of the form $\{p, p + 2, p + 6, p + 8\}$.
This is the only prime constellation of length 4. The first prime quadruplets are
$\{5, 7, 11, 13\}$, $\{11, 13, 17, 19\}$, $\{101, 103, 107, 109\}$, and $\{191, 193, 197, 199\}$.

*References:*
- [Prime quadruplet Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/prime_quadruplet)
- [List of unsolved problems in mathematics Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Prime quadruplets

A prime quadruplet is a set of four primes of the form $\{p, p + 2, p + 6, p + 8\}$.
This is the only prime constellation of length 4. The first prime quadruplets are
$\{5, 7, 11, 13\}$, $\{11, 13, 17, 19\}$, $\{101, 103, 107, 109\}$, and $\{191, 193, 197, 199\}$.

*References:*
- [Prime quadruplet Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/prime_quadruplet)
- [List of unsolved problems in mathematics Wikipedia page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace PrimeQuadruplet

/--
Are there infinitely many prime quadruplets? That is, are there infinitely many primes $p$
such that $p + 2$, $p + 6$ and $p + 8$ are also prime?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem prime_quadruplet :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      {p : ℕ | Prime p ∧ Prime (p + 2) ∧ Prime (p + 6) ∧ Prime (p + 8)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- The first prime quadruplet is $\{5, 7, 11, 13\}$. -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem prime_quadruplet_five :
    5 ∈ {p : ℕ | Prime p ∧ Prime (p + 2) ∧ Prime (p + 6) ∧ Prime (p + 8)} := by
  simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, ← Nat.prime_iff]
  norm_num

end PrimeQuadruplet

items: A prime quadruplet is taken, per the Wikipedia article, to be a set {p, p+2, p+6, p+8} of four primes (the only prime constellation of length 4); it is identified with its least element p, so 'infinitely many quadruplets' becomes 'the set of such p is infinite'.

The first quadruplet {5, 7, 11, 13} is included (no restriction like p > 5 or the 30n+11 form is imposed), matching the article's list; a `category test` theorem `prime_quadruplet_five` checks 5 belongs to the set.
`Prime p` with `p : ℕ` elaborates to `_root_.Prime`, which agrees with `Nat.Prime` (`Nat.prime_iff`); this follows the sibling files TwinPrimes.lean and PrimeTriplets.lean.

The question form 'Are there infinitely many ...?' is rendered with `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` so that `answer(True)` is the conjectured positive answer, following CONTRIBUTING.md's preferred style for questions.

The article's Hardy–Littlewood asymptotic count, Brun's constant B₄, and the quintuplet/sextuplet questions are not part of the list-page statement and are excluded, as the decomposition table specifies.
Import is `FormalConjecturesUtil`, matching all 147 existing Wikipedia files (AGENTS.md mentions `FormalConjectures.Util.ProblemImports`, which does not exist in this checkout).
